chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Uqba! Allah will not accept from the servants on the Day of Resurrection except this matter which you are upon. And there is nothing between one of you and seeing what delights his eyes except that his soul reaches to this,' and he gestured with his hand to the jugular vein, then reclined. And Mualla was with me, so he nudged me to ask him. I said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! When his soul reaches to this, what does he see?' I asked him 'What?' about ten times, and he said in all of them, 'He sees,' and did not add more to it.

Then he sat up at the end and said, 'O Uqba!' I said, 'At your service and happiness!' He said, 'Did you refuse except that I teach you?' I said, 'Yes, O son of the Messenger of Allah! My religion is with your religion. So when my religion departs, how will it be for me with you, O son of the Messenger of Allah, every moment?' And I cried, so he was sympathetic to me and said, 'He sees them both, by Allah.' I said, 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you! Who are they?'

He said, 'That is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and Ali (peace be upon him). O Uqba! A believing soul will never die until it sees them both.' I said, 'So when the believer looks at them both, does he return to the world?' He said, 'No, he goes ahead when he looks at them in front of him.' I said to him, 'Do they say anything?' He said, 'Yes. They both enter upon the believer together, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sits at his head, and Ali (peace be upon him) at his feet.'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) leans over him and says, 'O friend of Allah! Receive glad tidings. I am the Messenger of Allah. I am better for you than what you left of the world.' Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) rises, and Ali (peace be upon him) stands until he leans over him and says, 'O friend of Allah! Receive glad tidings. I am Ali ibn Abi Talib, whom you used to love. Indeed, I shall benefit you.'

Then he said, 'Indeed, this is in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' I said, 'Where did Allah place me, may I be your ransom, in the Book of Allah?' He said, 'In Surah Yunus.' The words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Those who believed and were pious. For them is good news in the worldly life and in the Hereafter; there is no changing the words of Allah; that is the great achievement.'
ai.seo_question: What does a believer see at the moment of death according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia doctrine of *Barzakh* (the intermediate realm), where the soul of the believer is visited by the Prophet Muhammad and Imam Ali before the final departure of the soul, offering glad tidings (*Bushra*) and spiritual benefit. Imam al-Sadiq explicitly links this vision to Surah Yunus, interpreting the 'good news in this life and the Hereafter' as the immediate spiritual encounter with the Ahl al-Bayt, thereby affirming their unique intercessory role and the continuity of divine favor for the pious beyond death.
